subject: Death Valley salt flat lake
title: What If a Lake Appeared in Death Valley? In 2024 People Kayaked on It

scenes.text: What if a lake appeared in Death Valley? In 2024, people kayaked the hottest place on Earth.
Badwater Basin sits 282 feet below sea level, a salt flat that averages about two inches of rain a year.
scenes.keywords: cracked salt polygons desert heat haze

scenes.text: On August 20th, 2023, the remains of Hurricane Hilary dumped 2.2 inches in one day. A whole year's rain.
A February 2024 storm added 1.5 inches more. A lake six miles long, three miles wide and a foot deep filled the basin.
Rangers allowed kayaks for about four weeks. By March 4th, 40-mile-an-hour winds had spread the water too thin.
In the Ice Age, Lake Manly here was 100 miles long and 600 feet deep. Today's version evaporates in months.

description:
What if a lake formed in Death Valley? Badwater Basin, 282 feet below sea level, averages about two inches of rain a year, but Hurricane Hilary's remnants dropped 2.2 inches on 20 August 2023 and an atmospheric river added 1.5 inches in February 2024.
The result was a lake about six miles long, three miles wide and a foot deep; the National Park Service allowed kayaking for about four weeks before winds spread it too thin in early March 2024. Ice Age Lake Manly was about 100 miles long and up to 600 feet deep.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Rangers say the kayak drag marks and footprints left in the salt could stay visible for years. Would you have paddled it? And what should we run through next?
